Treat i"},{"id":"p3s3","text":"t as research code, not production-ready software. It may still contain bugs, and its coding style a"},{"id":"p3s4","text":"nd engineering practices may be inconsistent. Review and adapt it before using it in your own enviro"},{"id":"p3s5","text":"nment.
>
> We have adapted it for publication, so it is not identical to our internal version or the"},{"id":"p3s6","text":" implementation described in *Exploring Super-agent Design: Towards a More Autonomous Agent System*."},{"id":"p3s7","text":" Some designs discussed in the article are directions for future development and are not implemented"},{"id":"p3s8","text":"ssed in the article are directions for future development and are not implemented in this prototype."},{"id":"p4s1","text":"dsh-superagent is a proactive coding agent for one GitHub repository, packaged as a bundle for DeepS"},{"id":"p4s2","text":"eek Harness. It listens to GitHub and, optionally, Feishu. When someone allowed asks the agent for w"},{"id":"p4s3","text":"ork, it opens a work item, works on it in its own agent session and directory, and answers in the or"},{"id":"p4s4","text":"iginal conversation, for example with a pull request. A web panel shows what needs a person."},{"id":"p5s1","text":"## This fork: work from your own machine"},{"id":"p6s1","text":"This repository is a fork of dsh-superagent that serves
**the person sitting at the machine** instea"},{"id":"p6s2","text":"d of a GitHub repository. Four things differ from upstream:"},{"id":"p7s1","text":"- **A local Source.** `src/sources/dsh.ts` (exported as `./local-watch`) turns a message in the main"},{"id":"p7s2","text":"
Session into a Trigger, and sends the answer back to that same Session. `source.kind === 'user'` is"},{"id":"p7s3","text":"
the filter, so messages that the orchestrator injects itself never loop back in.
- **One main Sessi"},{"id":"p7s4","text":"on per workspace.** Every sidebar workspace has its own orchestrator, created on
demand and remember"},{"id":"p7s5","text":"ed in `KV.runtime.masters` (workspaceId to sessionId). `GET
/orchestrator/api/master?workspace=<id>`"},{"id":"p7s6","text":" returns it, creating it when missing.
- **A sidebar entry.** The client half injects a star button "},{"id":"p7s7","text":"into each workspace group row
(`[data-row-key^="workspace:"]`), opens that workspace's main Session,"},{"id":"p7s8","text":" and hides main-session rows
from the list.
- **Attachments.** Images and files travel with the requ"},{"id":"p7s9","text":"est: the Trigger carries
`meta.attachments`, and the Worker receives the attachment-store path so it"},{"id":"p7s10","text":" can open the file
before deciding anything."},{"id":"p8s1","text":"It also runs without GitHub: `resolveDeployment` returns an empty repository when no remote is
confi"},{"id":"p8s2","text":"gured, and the GitHub watcher reports `paused` instead of polling."},{"id":"p9s1","text":"When an operator asks for work, the main Session routes it into a Ticket and a Worker does it in tha"},{"id":"p9s2","text":"t
workspace's directory; the main Session never edits files itself."},{"id":"p10s1","text":"It is also a way of working with an agent: **take as little human attention as possible, and give as"},{"id":"p10s2","text":" much value as possible.** An agent that can act for a whole team can also waste a whole team's atte"},{"id":"p10s3","text":"ntion, so it acts only when asked or when a rule the team wrote allows it, and speaks only when some"},{"id":"p10s4","text":"one must act or can use a result. docs/000-philosophy.md explains the principle and what it asks of "},{"id":"p10s5","text":"or can use a result. docs/000-philosophy.md explains the principle and what it asks of the operator."},{"id":"p11s1","text":"## Install"},{"id":"p12s1","text":"This bundle is not published to npm. Install it from the repository or from a prebuilt tarball:"},{"id":"p13s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p14s1","text":"Then follow SETUP.md for the profile configuration and the first start."},{"id":"p15s1","text":"## Setup"},{"id":"p16s1","text":"Setup has many steps, so an agent does it with you. Ask your coding agent:"},{"id":"p17s1","text":"> Read SETUP.md in this repository and set up dsh-superagent with me."},{"id":"p18s1","text":"It asks one short question at a time, shows the full plan once, and then installs and configures eve"},{"id":"p18s2","text":"rything. SETUP.md is what it follows."},{"id":"p19s1","text":"## Documentation"},{"id":"p20s1","text":"Read the numbered documents in order; each builds only on the ones before it."},{"id":"p21s1","text":"- 000 Philosophy
- 001 Domain model
- 002 Authorization
- 003 Execution
- 004 Prompts
- 005 Panel

- 007 Architecture
- 008 C"},{"id":"p21s3","text":"ookbook: adding a Source"},{"id":"p22s1","text":"## Development"},{"id":"p23s1","text":"`pnpm check` runs the typecheck, the tests and the build. `pnpm pack` produces the installable
bundl"},{"id":"p23s2","text":"e used by `dsh plugin add`. A fresh clone has no `lib/` (it is built, not committed); the
`prepare` "},{"id":"p23s3","text":"script builds it, so `pnpm install` is enough before starting the harness from source."},{"id":"p24s1","text":"## License"},{"id":"p25s1","text":"MIT"}],"truncated":false}
